A1.justification: Both PDFs describe SQL-R1 and contain readable main text, equations, tables, figures and appendices. Retained content can be matched reliably despite additions, relocation and renumbering.

before.justification: V1 reports original SQL-R1 benchmark results, cold-start comparisons and reward ablations in Tables 1–3, plus reasoning examples in Appendix A.

after.justification: V2 retains those original experiments and adds model-size comparisons, additional benchmark results, inference and training ablations, and training curves.

M1.justification: The SFT/direct-RL alternatives, GRPO objective, four reward components and self-consistency selection procedure are unchanged. Additional model sizes and experimental controls do not introduce a revised algorithm; the original prompt contents are also retained.

E1.justification: V2 adds a generalization evaluation on Spider-DK, Spider-Syn and Spider-Realistic in Appendix B.1/Table 4, extending the original Spider/BIRD evaluation to additional database and query requirements. SynSQL training coverage is retained. The PDFs provide limited detail about the precise construction of these added benchmark variants.

E2.justification: Table 1 adds DTS-SQL, DeepRetrieval and Reasoning-SQL and removes MCTS-SQL with GPT-4o-mini; CHASE-SQL is retained in a different position. Figure 2 removes XiYan-SQL-32B. New comparisons also include SENSE, ROUTE, SQL-PaLM and PURPLE in Table 4, and Qwen3 thinking-mode models in Table 5.

E3.justification: V2 adds SQL-R1 configurations at 3B and 14B, 14B cold-start controls, a candidate-count sweep over 4, 8, 12, 16 and 20, and database-value inclusion versus omission during RL training. These extend the evaluation design. The retained 7B data subsets, learning rates, eight-candidate default and inference temperature of 0.8 are unchanged.

E4.justification: The original reward-component ablation and Appendix A cases are retained. V2 adds Spider-variant robustness tests, expanded model-size/cold-start analysis, tests of how accuracy depends on candidate count and database-value inclusion, and reward/response-length training diagnostics in Appendix B.

E5.justification: Neither version documents repeated-run counts, seeds, confidence intervals or a defined significance test. V2 calls the database-value effect statistically nonsignificant without supplying a test or uncertainty estimate. Its training traces do not define uncertainty intervals or repeated-run aggregation.

E6.justification: Table 1 retains SQL-R1-7B at 87.6/88.7/66.6 for Spider-Dev/Spider-Test/BIRD-Dev, while adding 3B and 14B results; the 14B row reports 86.7/88.1/67.1. OmniSQL-7B Spider-Dev changes from 81.6 to 85.5 in Tables 1–2. Tables 4–6 and Figures 9–10 add further outcomes. V2's 7B prose and Table 5 conflict with Tables 1–2, preventing those discrepancies from being interpreted as confirmed performance changes.

T1.justification: The GRPO objective and mathematical definitions of all four rewards are unchanged. V2 adds equation numbers to the reward formulas, but introduces no new assumptions, derivations, theorems or proofs.

C1.justification: The abstract raises the BIRD headline from 66.6% to 67.1% and removes the 7B-only qualification; 67.1% corresponds to the added 14B result. The central contributions—RL-based NL2SQL reasoning, synthetic-data training and explicit reasoning traces—remain unchanged.

C2.justification: Section 3.3 changes from asserting cold-start training is necessary to concluding it is not universally essential and depends on data origin and volume. Appendix B adds interpretations concerning smaller-model RL benefits, candidate diversity versus computational cost, and database-value omission. V2 also adds a limitation concerning restricted base-model coverage while retaining the SQLite limitation.

D1.justification: V2 newly supplies a GitHub repository URL on the title page. Existing hardware specifications, learning rates, preprocessing descriptions and SFT/RL prompt contents are retained. The PDFs establish the added access information, not the repository's contents.

R1.justification: V2 adds a substantial Related Works section covering NL2SQL workflows and RL-based reasoning, with additional literature on schema-aware parsing, enterprise tasks, tool use and multimodal reasoning. It also explicitly positions SQL-R1 against concurrent approaches such as Reasoning-SQL and DeepRetrieval. This substantially expands v1's introduction-based positioning.

P1.justification: The main-results and cold-start discussions are substantially rewritten, and the limitations are expanded. A dedicated Related Works section and a five-part analysis appendix reorganize the supporting narrative, moving prompt templates from Appendix B to C. The method, conclusion and original case-study text remain largely verbatim.

P2.justification: V2 expands Tables 1–2, adds Tables 4–6, and introduces a candidate-count plot and a six-panel training figure. Figure 2 is redrawn with three SQL-R1 model sizes and revised comparator membership. The unchanged reward table is relocated, while the retained prompt figures are moved and renumbered.

improvement.justification: Broader model and robustness comparisons strengthen empirical support, and Section 3.3 usefully replaces v1's blanket cold-start necessity claim with a qualified conclusion. These gains are limited by new reporting problems: Section 3.2 gives 63.1% for 7B BIRD accuracy versus Table 1's 66.6%, Table 5's 7B Spider entries disagree with Table 2, and Appendix B.4 asserts nonsignificance without statistical support. The revision provides a limited net improvement rather than uniformly more reliable evidence.
